title: Geography: The Human and Physical World (Student Edition)

sources.what: publisher table of contents (2018 marketing code SS18; units and chapters)
publisher program page for the 2018 edition

summary: A high-school world geography text that opens with four chapters of physical and human geography, then surveys the world region by region in eight regional units. Regional chapters typically treat physical geography, history and government, and the people, culture, and economy of each country or subregion.

toc.label: Unit 1
toc.title: The World
toc.covers: Foundations of physical and human geography applied in every later unit.

children.label: Chapter 1
children.title: How Geographers Look at the World
children.covers: The five themes and essential elements of geography, maps, globes, projections, and geographic tools such as GIS.

children.label: Chapter 2
children.title: The Physical World
children.covers: Earth's structure, plate tectonics, landforms, weathering and erosion, and the water cycle.

children.label: Chapter 3
children.title: Climates of the Earth
children.covers: Earth-sun relationships, weather vs climate, climate regions, and natural vegetation.

children.label: Chapter 4
children.title: The Human World
children.covers: Population and migration, culture, political systems, economic systems, and resources.

toc.label: Unit 2
toc.title: The United States and Canada
toc.covers: Physical geography, history, and human patterns of the two North American countries.

children.label: Chapter 5
children.title: The United States
children.covers: U.S. landforms, climate, resources, settlement history, regions, economy, and culture.

children.label: Chapter 6
children.title: Canada
children.covers: Canada's physical regions, history, bilingual culture, and economy.

toc.label: Unit 3
toc.title: Latin America
toc.covers: Physical and human geography of Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, and South America.

children.label: Chapter 7
children.title: Mexico
children.covers: Mexico's landforms, climates, history, culture, and economy.

children.label: Chapter 8
children.title: Central America and the Caribbean
children.covers: The isthmus and island nations, their colonial history, and economies.

children.label: Chapter 9
children.title: South America
children.covers: The Andes, the Amazon, the countries of South America, and their people and economies.

toc.label: Unit 4
toc.title: Europe
toc.covers: Physical geography, history, and present-day countries of Europe and Russia.

children.label: Chapter 10
children.title: Northern Europe
children.covers: The Nordic countries and their climates, resources, and societies.

children.label: Chapter 11
children.title: Northwestern Europe
children.covers: The British Isles, France, the Benelux countries, Germany, and the Alpine states.

children.label: Chapter 12
children.title: Southern Europe
children.covers: The Iberian, Italian, and Balkan Mediterranean countries.

children.label: Chapter 13
children.title: Eastern Europe
children.covers: The countries between Germany and Russia and their post-communist transitions.

children.label: Chapter 14
children.title: The Russian Core
children.covers: Russia's physical geography, history, government, and economy.

toc.label: Unit 5
toc.title: North Africa, Southwest Asia, and Central Asia
toc.covers: Arid lands, oil resources, religions, and conflicts across North Africa, the Middle East, and Central Asia.

children.label: Chapter 15
children.title: North Africa
children.covers: Egypt and the Maghreb, the Nile and Sahara, and their history and economies.

children.label: Chapter 16
children.title: The Eastern Mediterranean
children.covers: Turkey, Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Jordan, and the Palestinian territories.

children.label: Chapter 17
children.title: The Northeast
children.covers: Iran, Iraq, and neighbouring states of the region's northeast.

children.label: Chapter 18
children.title: The Arabian Peninsula
children.covers: Saudi Arabia, the Gulf states, Yemen, and Oman, and the role of oil.

children.label: Chapter 19
children.title: Central Asia
children.covers: The former Soviet Central Asian republics and Afghanistan.

toc.label: Unit 6
toc.title: Africa South of the Sahara
toc.covers: Physical regions, history, and development of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.label: Chapter 20
children.title: The Transition Zone
children.covers: The Sahel belt between North Africa and the rest of the continent, with its desertification and cultural crossroads.

children.label: Chapter 21
children.title: East Africa
children.covers: Countries of East Africa and the Horn, the Rift Valley, and their peoples and economies.

children.label: Chapter 22
children.title: West Africa
children.covers: Coastal and inland West African countries and their history and economies.

children.label: Chapter 23
children.title: Equatorial Africa
children.covers: The Congo Basin countries and their rain forest environment and resources.

children.label: Chapter 24
children.title: Southern Africa
children.covers: South Africa and its neighbours, including apartheid's legacy and mineral wealth.

toc.label: Unit 7
toc.title: South Asia
toc.covers: The Indian subcontinent's physical geography, monsoon climate, history, and countries.

children.label: Chapter 25
children.title: India
children.covers: India's landforms, monsoons, history, religions, government, and economy.

children.label: Chapter 26
children.title: Pakistan and Bangladesh
children.covers: The two nations formed from partition, their geography, and challenges.

children.label: Chapter 27
children.title: Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka
children.covers: The smaller mountain and island states of South Asia.

toc.label: Unit 8
toc.title: East Asia
toc.covers: Physical and human geography of China, Mongolia, Japan, and the Koreas.

children.label: Chapter 28
children.title: China and Mongolia
children.covers: China's regions, history, government, and economy, and Mongolia's steppe society.

children.label: Chapter 29
children.title: Japan
children.covers: Japan's island geography, natural hazards, history, and economy.

children.label: Chapter 30
children.title: North Korea and South Korea
children.covers: The divided peninsula and its contrasting governments and economies.

toc.label: Unit 9
toc.title: Southeast Asia and the Pacific World
toc.covers: Mainland and island Southeast Asia, Australia, New Zealand, and the Pacific islands.

children.label: Chapter 31
children.title: Southeast Asia
children.covers: Mainland and island nations of Southeast Asia and their colonial past and growing economies.

children.label: Chapter 32
children.title: Australia and New Zealand
children.covers: Physical geography, Indigenous peoples, settlement, and economies of the two countries.

children.label: Chapter 33
children.title: Oceania
children.covers: The Pacific islands of Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia.

notes: Unit and chapter titles are from the publisher's TOC; lesson titles were not found. The TOC carries a 2018 marketing code, matching this ISBN's 2018 edition. A 2013 edition (ISBN 9780076642885) also exists, with possibly different chapter splits.
